parsed.label: positive: words ending in -ing or -ed (present/past participle forms); negative: proper nouns (first names)
parsed.trigger_hypothesis: The neuron activates positively on present or past participle verb forms (ending in -ing or -ed) and negatively on proper nouns, especially first names.
parsed.output_hypothesis: The neuron's positive activation encourages the use of participle verb forms, while its negative activation discourages the generation of proper nouns (first names).
alternatives: The neuron triggers on words ending in 'ed' or 'ing' regardless of part of speech.
The neuron triggers on words related to movement or action.
parsed.adapter_changes: State A+1 consistently amplifies positive activations (e.g., W01, W02, W03, W16, W17, W18) and slightly reduces negative magnitudes; state D+1 reduces positive activations (e.g., W01, W02, W03, W16, W17, W18) but leaves negatives mostly unchanged.

proposed_tests.discriminates: proper noun first name vs. common noun
proper noun last name vs. first name
participle in narrative vs. factual context
proper noun in middle of sentence
proper noun vs. common noun with same letters
